title: Gopher spheres are first-class project components
summary: v0.2-dev7 projects the supplied Gopher sphere roll-up into the same ownership/request catalogue as runtime components, so an LLM may own and receive work for one sphere without claiming the larger executable component it documents.
invariants: Sphere ownership is independent from runtime/executable ownership.
Canonical sphere component IDs are sphere:<gopher-sphere-id>.
Exact runtime component IDs take precedence over convenience aliases; explicit sphere: IDs remain available for collisions.
Journal events store canonical component IDs even when a caller uses an alias.
Ownership, release, requests, component mailboxes, replies, receipts and unread counts apply uniformly to sphere components.
sphere.check with a sphere component must match the component sphereId or fail SPHERE_COMPONENT_MISMATCH before invoking Gopher.
Do not infer parent-component ownership from sphere filesystem location or subject matter.

provenance.claim: Composite catalogue contains runtime and first-class sphere components.
Qualification locks sphere identity, collision, ownership, request and release semantics.
